newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks set for strong New Year start.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks set for strong New Year start.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks look set to start the Year of the Ox on a strong note, with a stable interest rate outlook likely to prompt a buying spree after the Chinese New Year holiday, analysts said.

"It looks like we are set for a 'red' opening," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. The market labels a higher opening on the first day of the new year with the lucky colour red.

The Hong Kong stock market was closed last Thursday and Friday for the Lunar New Year holiday and during the three-day week preceding the break, the Hang Seng index rose 338.71 points, or 2.54 percent, to close at 13,660.50 on Wednesday.

"We are looking at 14,000 in the very short term," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International. "Sentiment is quite bullish now in view of the latest economic data coming out of the U.S."

While Hong Kong was celebrating the Lunar New Year, the U.S. Federal Reserve chose to leave interest rates unchanged at Wednesday's policy setting meeting and U.S. January jobs data released on Friday showed robust economic growth with low inflation.
January non-farm payrolls rose by 271,000 compared with forecasts of 237,000 new jobs, but average hourly wages rose to only US$12.06 compared with US$12.05 in December.
"I guess people will be quite relieved," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.

The Dow industrials rallied to within 27 points of their all-time closing high on the employment data, gaining 82.74 points on Friday to close at 6,855.80. The U.S. long bond jumped 23/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
"It looks like next week the Dow can set a new record. I am sure Hong Kong will set a new record in the short term," said Rossiter.
The intra-day record high for Hong Kong's blue chip index stands at 14,004.93 points, set on January 16 this year.
But analysts said profit-takers were likely to come out at 14,000 points. To move beyond that hurdle, Hong Kong companies would have to report strong 1996 results.

"Whether it will go beyond 14,000 and move to 14,500, another critical level, depends on the bottom lines of these companies -- how they report financial 1996 earnings and how they present their outlook for 1997," said Tang.
Bank of East Asia Ltd has already set the tone for solid earnings by the banking sector, reporting slightly higher-than-expected net profit growth of 14.5 percent for 1996, he added.
"Most of the banks will report more than 20 percent growth, so if there are any surprises then these bank stocks will be aggressively bought," said Tang.

Shares in heavyweight HSBC Holdings Plc, which is due to report its 1996 results on March 3, were bid up strongly in London on Friday, rising HK$5.20 to HK$190.95. "It could test HK$200 coming up to its results," said Rossiter.

Property counters should also report strong earnings for 1996 while utility stocks have been well supported by share deals involving China Light & Power Co Ltd and Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd, said Tang.
"Once these three major sub-indices start to move, then the market is going to take off and easily move beyond the 14,000 point level," he said.
Judging from the performance of Hong Kong stocks in London over the Chinese New Year holiday, a 100-point jump in the Hang Seng index could be expected at Monday's opening, said Tang.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London rose 111.01 points last Friday to 13,771.51.
